items.title: How Standard Bank Group automates AI risk assessment for generative AI
items.excerpt: Standard Bank Group automated the evidence behind its generative AI approval gates. Working with AWS Professional Services, the bank built an assessment in its own AWS account that scores each use case against international AI standards and its own policies using LLM-as-a-judge on Amazon Bedrock, giving risk committees consistent, traceable evidence.

explained.headline: Attacks escalate as strikes hit Baltic cargo ship and Poland

happened.text: A Russian cargo ship was hit by a Ukrainian drone and caught fire in the Baltic Sea.
Two Russian missiles and a drone crashed into Polish territory.

background.text: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Ukrainian forces partially destroyed the Kerch road bridge linking Russia to Crimea.
Finland joined the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation in 2023, dropping decades of military non-alignment.

matters.text: Petteri Orpo, the prime minister of Finland, said the war was spilling over into the country's immediate vicinity.
Mark Rutte, the secretary general of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, guaranteed that the alliance would defend every inch of Polish territory.
Volodymyr Zelensky, the president of Ukraine, stated that Russian president Vladimir Putin wanted a reason to escalate the conflict.

uncertain.text: Antti Hakkanen, the Finnish defence minister, stated that a suspected airspace violation by a Russian helicopter may be linked to rescue or monitoring operations for the damaged cargo ship.
Russia has not publicly commented on the drone strike involving the merchant vessel in the Gulf of Finland.

terms.definition: An international military alliance of European and North American nations established for collective defence.

A Russian exclave situated along the Baltic Sea between Poland and Lithuania.

explained.headline: Mexican special forces arrest cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores

happened.text: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores and seven others were detained by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa.
Seven suspects and four members of the Mexican army were killed during the operation.
The arrest triggered retaliatory violence, including armed clashes, roadblocks and vehicle fires in the region.

background.text: The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation accused him of flooding the United States with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other drugs.

matters.text: The United States is seeking the extradition of the arrested drug lord.
The operation forms part of wider efforts by Mexico to tackle drug-related crime under pressure from United States President Donald Trump.

uncertain.text: It was not immediately clear whether authorities would extradite the suspect to the United States.
Authorities offered few details about how law enforcement agencies in Mexico and the United States coordinated the operation.

sources.title: Closer EU ties will give UK say on Brussels decisions, says Ed Miliband
Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says

explained.headline: UK and EU reach landmark cooperation deal at Brussels summit

happened.text: The United Kingdom and the European Union agreed to a landmark deal in Brussels that includes scrapping most checks on British food exports and introducing a new youth mobility scheme.
Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband stated that the agreements will come into force regardless of whether the two sides reach a separate tuition fees agreement.
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch criticised the agreement as unfair, arguing that British farmers would have to follow rules set in Brussels.

background.text: Ed Miliband is the Foreign Secretary of the United Kingdom, and Andy Burnham serves as the Prime Minister.
Ursula von der Leyen serves as the President of the European Commission.

The international landscape has shifted significantly since the 2016 Brexit referendum, marked by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the United States distancing itself from Europe under Donald Trump.

matters.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated that the Treasury believes the agreement could boost the United Kingdom economy by up to seventeen billion pounds a year.
Ed Miliband argued that closer links will give the United Kingdom a say on decisions made by Brussels rather than leaving the country in a position of following rules without input.

uncertain.text: Any timeline for further integration, including potential discussions about the United Kingdom rejoining the European Union, remains unclear following the summit.
Negotiators have yet to resolve a proposal from the European Union to lower the level of tuition fees paid by European Union students studying in the United Kingdom.
Conservative opposition politicians stated that they would scrap the newly agreed deal if they win power.

terms.definition: A cabinet minister in charge of a government's foreign policy and international relations.
A reciprocal agreement allowing young citizens to live, work or study abroad in partner countries for a set period.
A market-based system aimed at reducing greenhouse gases by setting a limit on emissions and allowing entities to buy and sell allowances.

removed.text: Duncan Ivison, the vice chancellor of the University of Manchester, warned that allowing European Union students to pay domestic university fees could take five hundred million pounds out of the higher education sector.
why: The claim omits that the £500m figure is an estimate.
